For each integer \(n\ge2\), let \(\mathcal K_n\) consist of all sets \(K=\overline\Omega\subset\mathbb C^n\), where \(\Omega\) is a nonempty bounded connected open set with \(C^\infty\) boundary.

Use the following orientation convention for pseudoconvexity. Near each \(q\in\partial K\), take a smooth real defining function \(\rho\) with \(K\cap U=\{\rho\le0\}\) and \(d\rho\ne0\) on \(\partial K\cap U\). The boundary \(\partial K\) is pseudoconvex if, at every such \(q\),
\[
\sum_{j,k=1}^{n}\rho_{z_j\bar z_k}(q)v_j\overline{v_k}\ge0
\qquad\text{whenever}\qquad
\sum_{j=1}^{n}\rho_{z_j}(q)v_j=0.
\]

An open set \(Y\subset\mathbb C^n\) is called Oka if, for every integer \(m\ge1\), every nonempty compact convex set \(Q\subset\mathbb C^m\), every holomorphic map \(f:V\to Y\) on an open neighbourhood \(V\) of \(Q\), and every \(\varepsilon>0\), there is a holomorphic map \(F:\mathbb C^m\to Y\) satisfying
\[
\sup_{x\in Q}\|F(x)-f(x)\|<\varepsilon,
\]
where the norm is Euclidean.

Define the two sets of dimensions
\[
\begin{aligned}
S&=\bigl\{n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}:\ \text{for every }K\in\mathcal K_n,\quad
\partial K\text{ pseudoconvex}\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathbb C^n\setminus K\text{ Oka}\bigr\},\\
N&=\bigl\{n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}:\ \text{for every }K\in\mathcal K_n,\quad
\mathbb C^n\setminus K\text{ Oka}\ \Longrightarrow\ \partial K\text{ pseudoconvex}\bigr\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Determine exactly the ordered pair \((S,N)\).

import sympy as s
from pathlib import Path
# Symbolic Levi certificate for rho=(|z1|^2+|z2|^2-1)^2+sum |w_j|^2-eps.
x1,y1,x2,y2,u,v,eps=s.symbols('x1 y1 x2 y2 u v eps',real=True)
xs=[x1,x2,u]; ys=[y1,y2,v]
a=x1*x1+y1*y1+x2*x2+y2*y2
rho=(a-1)**2+u*u+v*v-eps
Dz=lambda f,j:(s.diff(f,xs[j])-s.I*s.diff(f,ys[j]))/2
Db=lambda f,j:(s.diff(f,xs[j])+s.I*s.diff(f,ys[j]))/2
g=s.Matrix([Dz(rho,j) for j in range(3)])
L=s.Matrix(3,3,lambda j,k:s.expand(Db(Dz(rho,j),k)))
z=s.Matrix([x1+s.I*y1,x2+s.I*y2]); w=u+s.I*v
# holomorphic tangent vector, nonzero at every boundary point for eps<1/4
T=s.Matrix([s.conjugate(w)*z[0],s.conjugate(w)*z[1],-2*(a-1)*a])
assert s.expand((g.T*T)[0])==0
levi=s.expand((T.T*L*s.conjugate(T))[0])
expected=(4*a-2)*a*(u*u+v*v)+4*(a-1)**2*a*a

from pathlib import Path
# Exact local peak identity for the model strictly pseudoconvex domain B^n.
# q=(1,0,...,0), h(z)=z_1-1.  This identity proves Re(h)<=-|z-q|²/2

lam=s.symbols('lam',positive=True)
r=(w+wb)/2+lam*z*zb
L=s.Matrix([[s.diff(r,a,b) for b in (zb,wb)] for a in (z,w)])
assert L==s.diag(lam,0)
assert s.diff(r,w)==s.Rational(1,2)

import sympy as s
# Levi matrix of rho=(|z|^2-1)^2+||w||^2-2, in real coordinates at z=0,w=(1,0,...).
x,y,u,v=s.symbols('x y u v', real=True)
r=(x*x+y*y-1)**2+u*u+v*v-2
Lz=s.simplify((s.diff(r,x,2)+s.diff(r,y,2))/4)
Lw=s.simplify((s.diff(r,u,2)+s.diff(r,v,2))/4)
assert Lz == 4*(x*x+y*y)-2
assert Lw == 1
assert r.subs({x:0,y:0,u:1,v:0}) == 0
assert Lz.subs({x:0,y:0}) == -2
# For n>=3 add w2 direction: both z and w2 are tangent, eigenvalues -2,+1.
print('Exact candidate check: boundary rho=0 at (0,1,0,...), tangential Levi eigenvalues -2,+1 for n>=3.')
# Verify elementary positive-normal correction used by strict pseudoconvex peak proof:
a,b,c,A=s.symbols('a b c A', real=True)
H=s.Matrix([[a,b],[b,c+A]])
assert s.factor(H.det())==A*a+a*c-b*b
print('Schur correction det =',s.factor(H.det()),'; positive for a>0, A>b²/a-c.')

Shrinking the neighborhood keeps r+A r² negative precisely when r is negative. Taylor expansion at q=0 writes

Hence it is not constant, contradiction.

import sympy as s
from pathlib import Path
x,y,z,X,Y,Z,a,M,r=s.symbols('x y z X Y Z a M r', nonzero=True)
H=s.Matrix([a*y+M*x*x,a*z+M*y*y,a*x])
xinv=Z/a
yinv=(X-M*xinv*xinv)/a
zinv=(Y-M*yinv*yinv)/a
Hi=s.Matrix([xinv,yinv,zinv])
assert all(s.simplify(expr-target)==0 for expr,target in zip(H.subs({x:xinv,y:yinv,z:zinv}, simultaneous=True),[X,Y,Z]))
assert s.simplify(H.jacobian([x,y,z]).det()-a**3)==0

assert A**3==a**3*s.eye(3)
# For a=1/2,M>=2,r>=2, r_next>=M*r²-a*r>2*r.

entry=s.simplify(((4*R+4)/d**2)*d**2-s.Rational(1,2)*R)
assert s.simplify(entry-(s.Rational(7,2)*R+4))==0
print('PASS generalized Henon inverse/Jacobian/attracting linear part/escape-cone bounds')

## Outer approximation lemma (proved)
Suppose n>=3 and K is the closure of a bounded domain with C-infinity pseudoconvex boundary. Then K has a decreasing neighborhood basis K_epsilon of compact domains with smooth boundary having a strictly positive tangential Levi direction at each point.

Choose a smooth signed-distance defining function rho in a fixed collar of boundary K, negative on K. Compactness, smoothness, and pseudoconvexity imply a constant C with
L_rho(z;v) >= -C rho(z)||v||²
for all z in the outer collar and v in ker(partial rho(z)). To see this, project z to its nearest boundary point q; rho(z) is the signed distance. The tangent hyperplanes and Levi matrices differ by O(rho(z)); projecting v to ker(partial rho(q)) changes it by O(rho(z))||v||. Apply nonnegativity at q and absorb the uniform errors.

Fix A>C and set psi_epsilon(z)=rho(z)-epsilon exp(-A||z||²) in the collar. For sufficiently small epsilon, its zero set is a unique small positive outward normal graph over boundary K, since its outward normal derivative is uniformly positive. Define K_epsilon to be K plus the part of the outer collar where psi_epsilon<=0. These are smooth compact connected domains, decrease to K as epsilon decreases to zero, and form a neighborhood basis.

At a boundary point z of K_epsilon, rho(z)=epsilon exp(-A||z||²). The complex subspace
E_z=ker(partial rho(z)) intersect ker(partial ||z||²)
has dimension at least n-2>=1. Every nonzero v in E_z is complex tangent to psi_epsilon=0. Direct differentiation gives
L_{-exp(-A||z||²)}(v)=exp(-A||z||²)[A||v||²-A²|sum bar(z_j)v_j|²].
The final term vanishes on E_z, so
L_{psi_epsilon}(v)>=epsilon exp(-A||z||²)(A-C)||v||²>0.

The exteriors C^n minus K_epsilon increase to C^n minus K. Hence any theorem asserting Oka for holes with one strictly positive tangential Levi direction would imply the desired universal sufficiency in every n>=3, since increasing unions of Oka domains are Oka directly by CAP compactness. No such global theorem is proved in this note.

from pathlib import Path
from z3 import Int, Real, Solver, Or, If, sat, unsat
import sympy as s

# At an infinity branch, p>0, 0<=q<=p. Under H, p'=q.
# If p!=2q, there is no cancellation and q'=max(p,2q).
# The K+ cone bound requires q'<=p'=q, which is impossible.
p,q,qp=Int('p'),Int('q'),Int('qp')
solver=Solver()
solver.add(p>0,q>0,q<=p,p!=2*q,qp==If(p>2*q,p,2*q),qp<=q)
assert solver.check()==unsat

# If q=0 initially, p'=0 while q'=p>0, also impossible.
solver=Solver()
solver.add(p>0,q==0,qp==p,qp<=q)
assert solver.check()==unsat

# Escape cone inequality for H(z,w)=(w/10,z/10+10w^2).
# If r=|w|>max(|z|,2), then |w'| >=10r^2-r/10 >2r.
r=s.symbols('r', positive=True)
assert s.factor(10*r*r-r/s.Integer(10)-2*r)==r*(100*r-21)/10
assert 100*s.Integer(2)-21>0

# The forced order p_j=2q_j and p_{j+1}=q_j imply p_{j+1}=p_j/2.
# Finite induction is symbolic: p_j = p_0/2^j.
j=s.symbols('j', integer=True, nonnegative=True)
p0=s.symbols('p0',integer=True,positive=True)
assert s.simplify((p0/2**j)/2-p0/2**(j+1))==0
print('UNSAT checks passed: every infinity-branch iteration forces positive pole order to halve.')
print('This confirms the algebraic core of the proof that the attracting Henon basin contains no ambient-closed analytic curves.')
Path('workspace/agent3_henon_no_curve_checks.py').write_text(Path('scratchpad.py').read_text().split("Path('workspace/agent3_henon_no_curve_checks.py')")[0])

from pathlib import Path
text = r'''# A Fatou--Bieberbach domain with no ambient-closed analytic curves

Let H(z,w)=(w/10,z/10+10w^2). Its derivative at zero has eigenvalues +/-1/10, so zero is attracting, and its basin is biholomorphic to C^2 by the standard attracting-basin theorem.

If |w|>max(|z|,2), then |w'|>=10|w|^2-|z|/10>2|w| and |z'|=|w|/10. Thus this cone is forward invariant and escaping. The forward nonescaping set K+ is contained in {|w|<=max(|z|,2)}.

Suppose A is an ambient-closed irreducible analytic curve contained in K+. Projection to z is proper, since over bounded z the inequality bounds w, and it has finite fibers, since a vertical curve component would be compact. The monic Weierstrass polynomial of this finite covering has coefficients entire in z, and its coefficient of degree d-j in w has growth O((1+|z|)^j). Therefore all coefficients are polynomials; A is algebraic.

Choose a point at infinity of its compact normalization. Let p_j,q_j denote pole orders of the two coordinates of H^j on this branch, with order zero for functions bounded at this point. The cone bound gives 0<=q_j<=p_j. Properness of polynomial automorphism H implies at least one coordinate has a pole after every iterate, hence p_j>0. If q_j=0, then z_{j+1}=w_j/10 is bounded but w_{j+1}=z_j/10+10w_j^2 has pole order p_j, contradicting the cone bound. Therefore q_j>0.

Now p_{j+1}=q_j. If p_j != 2q_j, the pole order of w_{j+1} is max(p_j,2q_j)>q_j=p_{j+1}, another contradiction. Thus p_j=2q_j for every j, giving p_{j+1}=p_j/2 indefinitely. Positive integers cannot satisfy this recurrence. No A exists.

Consequently, if F:C^2 -> Omega is a biholomorphism, the globally strictly plurisubharmonic function ||F||^2 on C^2 is unbounded but admits no nonconstant holomorphic curve proper with respect to it. Such a curve would give an ambient-proper map into C^2 and hence an ambient-closed analytic curve in Omega by Remmert's theorem.

This blocks a speculative proof route; it does NOT settle the user's dimension sets.
'''

from pathlib import Path
import mpmath as mp
import sympy as s

note=r'''# An explicit smooth pseudoconvex worm compact with no Stein neighborhood basis

This note proves geometry only. It does **not** claim that the complement is non-Oka.

## 1. The defining function

Put
\[
\chi(s)=\begin{cases}
0,&s\leq0,\\
\displaystyle\int_0^s(s-u)e^{-1/u}\,du,&s>0,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\eta(t)=\chi(-t)+\chi(t-2\pi).
\]
The standard flat function $e^{-1/s}$, extended by zero for $s\leq0$, is smooth. Thus $\chi$ is smooth, convex, flat at zero, strictly increasing for $s>0$, and unbounded. For instance, for $s\geq1$,
\[
\chi(s)\geq \tfrac12e^{-1}(s-1)^2.
\]
Consequently $\eta$ is smooth and convex, vanishes exactly on $[0,2\pi]$, and tends to infinity at both ends. There is a unique $a>0$ with $\chi(a)=1$, and
\[
\{t:\eta(t)<1\}=(-a,2\pi+a).
\]
On $\mathbb C\times\mathbb C^*$ define $t=\log|w|^2$ and
\[
\rho(z,w)=|z-e^{it}|^2-1+\eta(t)
=|z|^2-ze^{-it}-\bar z e^{it}+\eta(t).
\]
Let $\Omega=\{\rho<0\}$ and $K=\overline\Omega$.

## 2. Membership in the class $\mathcal K_2$

Every point of $\Omega$ satisfies
\[
e^{-a/2}<|w|<e^{\pi+a/2},\qquad |z|<2.
\]
Thus the set is bounded and stays away from $w=0$. It is nonempty, since $(z,w)=(1,1)$ has $\rho=-1$. Its base in the $w$ variable is the connected annulus displayed above. Every fiber is the nonempty disc
\[
|z-e^{i\log|w|^2}|<\sqrt{1-\eta(\log|w|^2)}.
\]
Fiberwise recentering and rescaling gives a homeomorphism with the product of this base annulus and the unit disc. In particular, $\Omega$ is connected.

Writing $u=ze^{-it}=x+iy$, direct differentiation gives
\[
\rho_z=\bar z-e^{-it},\qquad
\rho_w=\frac{\eta'(t)-2y}{w}.
\]
If $\rho_z=0$ on the boundary, then $z=e^{it}$ and $\eta(t)=1$. At either such level $\eta'(t)\ne0$, so $\rho_w\ne0$. Hence $d\rho\ne0$ everywhere on $\{\rho=0\}$. All points of this regular zero set are boundary points of $\{\rho<0\}$, so $K=\{\rho\leq0\}$. The preceding compact bounds and regularity prove $K\in\mathcal K_2$.

## 3. Oriented Levi pseudoconvexity

The complex Hessian is
\[
\rho_{z\bar z}=1,\qquad
\rho_{z\bar w}=\frac{i e^{-it}}{\bar w},\qquad
\rho_{w\bar z}=\frac{-i e^{it}}{w},\qquad
\rho_{w\bar w}=\frac{\eta''(t)+2x}{|w|^2}.
\]
The nonzero vector $T=(\rho_w,-\rho_z)$ spans the complex tangent line. Put $d=\eta'-2y$. On the boundary,
\[
x^2+y^2-2x+\eta=0,
\qquad |\rho_z|^2=(x-1)^2+y^2=1-\eta.
\]
A direct calculation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
|w|^2\mathcal L_\rho(T)
&=d^2+2dy+(\eta''+2x)((x-1)^2+y^2)\\
&=(\eta'-y)^2+(x-\eta)^2
  +\eta(1-\eta)+\eta''(1-\eta)\geq0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Indeed $0\leq\eta\leq1$ on the boundary and $\eta''\geq0$. Thus the boundary is pseudoconvex with precisely the orientation in the problem. The polynomial identity is checked in `agent2_worm_levi.py` and independently in `agent3_worm_identity_check.py`.

## 4. A fixed exterior point belongs to every Stein neighborhood

For $c\in[0,1]$ consider the holomorphic annulus
\[
A_c=\{(c,w):1\leq|w|\leq e^\pi\}.
\]
The initial annulus $A_0$ lies in $K$: its logarithmic radii have $t\in[0,2\pi]$, so $\eta=0$ and $\rho(0,w)=0$. The two boundary circles of every $A_c$ lie in $K$, since at $t=0$ and $t=2\pi$,
\[
\rho(c,w)=c^2-2c\leq0.
\]
However,
\[
p=(1,e^{\pi/2})\in A_1,\qquad \rho(p)=3>0.
\]

Let $U$ be any Stein open neighborhood of $K$, and choose a continuous plurisubharmonic exhaustion $\Phi$ of $U$. Put $M=\max_K\Phi$. The set
\[
J=\{c\in[0,1]:A_c\subset U\}
\]
is relatively open and contains zero. Whenever $c\in J$, the subharmonic maximum principle on the annulus gives $\Phi\leq M$ on $A_c$, because its boundary lies in $K$. Hence all such annuli lie in the fixed compact subset $\{\Phi\leq M\}\Subset U$. If $c_j\in J$ tends to $c$, this compact containment implies $A_c\subset U$, so $J$ is also relatively closed. Connectedness of $[0,1]$ gives $J=[0,1]$. In particular $p\in U$.

Thus every Stein neighborhood of $K$ contains the fixed point $p\notin K$. Taking the neighborhood $\mathbb C^2\setminus\{p\}$ shows that $K$ has no Stein neighborhood basis.

## 5. The same point belongs to the rational hull: a direct argument-principle proof

Let $P$ be a polynomial nonvanishing on $K$. For every $c\in[0,1]$, the polynomial $w\mapsto P(c,w)$ is nonzero on the two boundary circles of the annulus $1\leq|w|\leq e^\pi$. Its number of zeros in the annulus, counted with multiplicity, is the difference of its two boundary winding numbers. This integer is constant in $c$, since neither boundary circle acquires a zero. It is zero at $c=0$, as $A_0\subset K$. Therefore it is zero for all $c$, and in particular $P(p)\ne0$.

Equivalently, every polynomial vanishing at $p$ has a zero on $K$. This is exactly $p\in h_r(K)$, the rational hull of $K$. Hence $K$ is not rationally convex.

## Scope

The note establishes an explicit $K\in\mathcal K_2$ with pseudoconvex boundary and no Stein neighborhood basis, together with a specified exterior rational-hull point. It does not establish any obstruction to the Oka property of $\mathbb C^2\setminus K$. Such an obstruction remains a separate missing theorem in the team's work.
'''
Path('workspace/agent3_worm_geometry.md').write_text(note)
# Independent algebraic checks of the boundary values used in Sections 2 and 4.
c=s.symbols('c',real=True)
assert s.expand((c-1)**2-1-(c*c-2*c))==0
assert (1-(-1))**2-1==3
x,y,eta,e1,e2=s.symbols('x y eta e1 e2',real=True)
d=e1-2*y
numerator=d*d+2*d*y+(e2+2*x)*((x-1)**2+y*y)
positive=(e1-y)**2+(x-eta)**2+eta*(1-eta)+e2*(1-eta)
assert s.rem(s.Poly(s.expand(numerator-positive),x),s.Poly(x*x+y*y-2*x+eta,x)).as_expr()==0
# Numerical illustration only; existence/uniqueness and bounds above are analytic.
mp.mp.dps=35
def chi(v):
    if v<=0:return mp.mpf(0)
    return mp.quad(lambda u:(v-u)*mp.exp(-1/u),[0,v])
a=mp.findroot(lambda v:chi(v)-1,(2,4))
assert abs(chi(a)-1)<mp.mpf('1e-30')
print('Worm geometry note saved; boundary and Levi identities checked.')
print('Illustrative a with chi(a)=1:',a)
print('w radius bounds:',mp.exp(-a/2),mp.exp(mp.pi+a/2))

Move p to zero and L to {x=y=0}; write coordinates (x,y,z_1,...,z_{n-2}). Put a=1/2. Set
H(x,y,z_1,z_2,...)= (a y+M x², a z_1+M y², a x, a z_2,...).
This is a polynomial automorphism: solve successively x=z'_1/a, y=(x'-Mx²)/a, z_1=(y'-My²)/a, z_j=z'_j/a. Its derivative at zero is A=aP, P unitary (a 3-cycle plus fixed coordinates).

Take R>=1 bounding the absolute values of all coordinates on K, and delta=min_K max(|x|,|y|)>0. Choose M=2+(4R+4)/delta². The first image of K has foreground maximum r'=max(|x'|,|y'|)>=M delta²-aR=2delta²+3.5R+4, while all background coordinates have absolute value <=aR. Hence H(K) lies in
C={max(|x|,|y|)>max(2,2 max_j|z_j|)}.
On C, if r=max(|x|,|y|), then r_next>=Mr²-ar>2r, and background_next<=ar. Thus C is forward invariant and every point of H(K) escapes to infinity. The attracting basin B of zero is therefore disjoint from K.

For completeness, B is biholomorphic to C^n without invoking a separate basin theorem. Choose a<b<sqrt(a). For a sufficiently small neighborhood U of zero, ||H(x)||<=b||x|| and ||H(x)-Ax||<=C||x||². The maps phi_k=A^{-k}H^k converge uniformly on a smaller neighborhood because
||phi_{k+1}-phi_k||<=C a^{-1}(b²/a)^k ||x||².
The limit phi is holomorphic, Dphi(0)=I, and phi H=A phi. Shrink U so phi is injective and H(U) subset U. Extend phi to B by phi(x)=A^{-k}phi(H^k(x)) once H^k(x) lies in U. This extension is well-defined, holomorphic, and injective. Its image contains every A^{-k}phi(U), whose union is C^n since phi(U) contains a ball and A is a strict scalar contraction times a unitary matrix. Thus phi:B→C^n is biholomorphic. Its inverse, followed by the original coordinate change, is the asserted Phi.

Application: the compact mixed Hartogs domain K={(z,w):(|z|²-1)²+||w||²<=2}, z in C, w in C^{n-1}, has an avoiding affine (n-2)-plane through every exterior point. At a fixed base z, its nonempty fiber is a ball. Therefore the exterior is strongly dominable everywhere.

This is NOT a CAP/Oka proof: no holomorphic family of the avoiding planes or charts along an arbitrary convex-source map has been constructed.
